reconcile.note: Adam Clarke resolves the fear-versus-faith tension by reading Hebrews as describing Moses' later, bold departure at the Exodus rather than his fearful flight to Midian.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013).

sides.snippet: Moses was afraid, and said, \"Surely this thing is known.\"
sides.verseText: He said, \"Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian?\" Moses was afraid, and said, \"Surely this thing is known.\"

sides.snippet: By faith, he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
sides.verseText: By faith, he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
